title: Backstage Update - WWE NXT Pay - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Clark ,
3 minutes ago
There’s been plenty of debate recently about pay in WWE NXT, particularly from former talent who were recently released. However, a new report suggests that some of those claims might not tell the full story.
On the latest edition of Wrestling Observer Live, Bryan Alvarez pushed back on the idea that NXT wrestlers are severely underpaid, offering some clarity about developmental contracts.
According to Alvarez, “confirmed NXT deals start at $75,000,” though he added that “big-name talent brought in from the outside obviously make more than that.” He also refuted suggestions that anyone on the roster earns an extremely low salary, stating, “Nobody is making $30,000.”
READ MORE: Edris Enofe Is Officially Gone From WWE
READ MORE: Chavo Guerrero Has Officially Re-Signed With WWE
That $30,000 figure came from Priscilla Kelly (Gigi Dolin), who discussed pay in a recent interview with Denise Salcedo of Instinct Culture. She said,
“The common misconception about NXT performers is that we’re millionaires. A lot of fans think that if you work in WWE, you live in a mansion, you’re driving a Mercedes, you’ve got it made. That’s not the case. In NXT, there are contracts as low as $30,000 a year, and they don’t go as high as people think.”
It is said that there is one group in the system that makes considerably less — WWE’s ID talent. These individuals aren’t signed to official TKO contracts and are instead paid small amounts to assist with their development. Alvarez stated, “ID talent make much less than $30,000, but they aren’t under an official contractual salaried deal. They’re paid a small amount to help upgrade their look, etc.”
